headline: The Thanksgiving storm is on track: 1.5 to 2 inches of rain (locally up to 3), damaging wind gusts around 40 to 60 mph in New York City and Long Island, and widespread moderate coastal flooding at both Thursday high tides, with the worst Thursday afternoon and evening.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Wednesday night starts dry around New York City as high pressure to the north holds on, but low clouds develop over the city and along the coast by around midnight and spread north toward morning. East-northeast winds ramp up after midnight, reaching about 25 to 30 mph with gusts of 35 to 40 mph by the Thursday morning commute.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Thanksgiving brings the storm, with the heaviest rain and strongest winds most likely Thursday afternoon and evening, though the latest short-range model hints the peak winds could arrive 2 to 3 hours later than forecast. A High Wind Warning runs from 10 AM Thursday to 1 AM Friday for New York City, Long Island and the Hudson, eastern Essex and eastern Union county areas of New Jersey, with gusts of roughly 40 to 60 mph and possibly higher Thursday evening; a Wind Advisory from 10 AM Thursday to 5 AM Friday covers the rest of northeast New Jersey, Westchester, Rockland, Orange, Putnam and southern Connecticut. Moist air from the subtropics brings 1.5 to 2 inches of rain in general with local amounts up to 3 inches, heavy downpours at times and an isolated thunderstorm possible Thursday evening. The rain tapers from southwest to northeast after about 9 PM Thursday and winds turn southerly and ease after 1 AM, though light rain or drizzle may linger; Friday brings scattered showers and a breezy southwest wind gusting about 30 to 35 mph, turning west Friday night.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Saturday looks dry with west winds gusting about 25 to 30 mph, easing at night, and Sunday stays quiet. Showers are likely late Sunday night, with a chance of showers lingering Monday morning and southwest gusts around 25 to 30 mph turning west in the afternoon and northwest Monday night. The discussion gives no temperature details for these days.

coast: Gale- to storm-force east-northeast winds Thursday morning into Thursday night, on top of already-high tides after the recent full moon, make widespread moderate coastal flooding likely at both the Thursday morning and evening high tides, with potential for major flooding along the western Great South Bay and significant impacts around Peconic Bay and the Peconic River and along the western Long Island Sound shoreline; surge up the Hackensack, Hudson and Passaic rivers brings minor to moderate flooding. Thursday morning's tide is naturally higher by at least a foot, but the peak surge is expected Thursday afternoon and evening, so both tides may reach similar levels, and heavy rain during the evening tide could worsen coastal street flooding; forecasters leaned toward the higher-end water levels for a safety margin. Coastal Flood Warnings run 7 AM Thursday to 6 AM Friday for New York City, Long Island, northeast New Jersey's waterfront, southern Westchester and southwestern Connecticut (southern Middlesex and New London counties are under an advisory through 3 PM Friday). For Friday's morning high tide, the earlier watch is now a Coastal Flood Advisory for the north shore of Long Island, New York City (except southern Queens), northeast New Jersey, Westchester and southwestern Connecticut, where water should drain out and impacts be mainly minor, while a Coastal Flood Watch stays up for southern Queens, southern Nassau and southern Suffolk, where southwest winds could bring another round of moderate flooding, especially on the eastern Great South Bay. Ocean beaches see 8 to 12 foot breakers with widespread beach flooding, dune erosion and possible localized overwash; western Long Island Sound and the Twin Forks see 3 to 6 foot waves with dune erosion, splashover and possible isolated damage to shoreline and marina structures. On the water, a Gale Warning until 6 AM Thursday gives way to a Storm Warning from 6 AM Thursday to 1 AM Friday, with ocean seas over 20 feet late Thursday afternoon and evening and waves near 10 feet on the Sound and at the New York Harbor entrance; a southwest gale is likely on the ocean Friday, easing to small-craft-advisory levels Saturday and below that Sunday, with small-craft conditions possible again Monday.

confidence: Models agree well on the Thursday storm, with a few hours of uncertainty in the timing of peak winds, and the coastal flood forecast deliberately leans toward the higher end; the weekend and Monday get little detail.
